children: Robusta coffee futures on ICE rose on Thursday, recovering from recent three-year lows as farmers in top grower Vietnam were said to be looking at holding back supplies if prices keep falling.
London cocoa and white sugar hit near one-month peaks.
There was no trading in arabica coffee, raw sugar and New York cocoa due to the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States.
COFFEE
* Robusta coffee
rose 1.5% to $2,809 a metric ton by 1312 GMT, after setting a 3-year low of $2,709 on Wednesday.
* Prices have been falling steadily as what is expected to be a bumper harvest gets underway in Vietnam.
* However, market participants on the ground say farmers are likely to hold back supplies if prices fall below 70,000-72,000 dong ($2.71-2.79) per kg.
* Arabica coffee
closed up 2.8% at $2.70 per lb on Wednesday, after earlier hitting a 5-month low.
SUGAR
* White sugar
was 0.9% higher at $521.60 a ton, having earlier hit its highest since late October at $523.80.
* Sugar production in India, the world's second-largest producer, is expected to fall to decade lows in the 2026/27 season.

* The Supreme Court in India, also the world's largest sugar consumer, has ruled that a government labelling proposal for food packaging should require separate labels to indicate high amounts of salt, sugar and fat in foods, not just a single one as proposed earlier.
* The US, the world's third-largest sugar consumer and importer, has proposed a new tariff of 20 cents per pound for sugar imports of all origins.
* Raw sugar (SBH7) settled up 3.9% at 18.34 cents per lb on Wednesday.
COCOA
* London cocoa
was down 0.2% at £4,219 per ton, having hit its highest since early November at £4,247.
* Dealers said the supply outlook continues to worsen in top growers Ivory Coast, Ghana and Ecuador. However, there has been some origin selling from those countries, which is keeping gains in check.
* There is also ample availability of cocoa from the bumper 2025/26 crop.

* Ghana’s cocoa regulator Cocobod said it was recalling a liquid fertiliser distributed in the Central Region after farmers alleged the product had expired, the latest challenge for the sector after a poor start to the season.
* New York cocoa
closed up 0.4% at $5,434 a ton on Wednesday.
